extraction_warnings: This is a large metagenomic assembly study with 9,428+ samples from multiple studies and cohorts. Individual sample-level metadata is not provided in the paper body but referenced in Table S1 and curatedMetagenomicData package. Sample-level extraction would require access to supplementary tables.
The paper does not report individual subject or sample IDs within the main text; these are referenced as being available in supplementary resources.
Age data is reported as age groups and ranges for aggregate cohorts, not as individual values.
The Ethiopia cohort sample size is very small (5 individuals) and appears female-only based on the brief mention.
Family relationships (mother-infant pairs) are mentioned for validation studies but not systematically documented for all participants.
The paper combines data from 46 different public studies with varying metadata completeness; harmonized metadata is in the curatedMetagenomicData package.

This is a metagenomic microbiome study focusing on reconstruction of 154,723 microbial genomes. Most clinical and demographic fields in the schema are not applicable or reported. The paper emphasizes microbial diversity across populations, body sites, ages, and lifestyles rather than individual-level clinical phenotypes.

Age information is reported at the cohort level in broad categories (newborns <1 year, children 1-12 years, school-age 12-19 years, adults 19-65 years, seniors >65 years), not as individual participant ages.
Madagascar cohort (112 individuals) is explicitly described as 'healthy volunteers'; other cohorts assembled from public datasets are not consistently described regarding health status.
Study includes maternal milk samples (n=9) but these are mentioned only in passing and no individual-level metadata is provided.
The schema targets clinical/phenotypic data that this genomic characterization paper does not systematically report for individual participants.

This paper is a microbiome genomics study focused on bacterial and archaeal genome reconstruction from human metagenomes. Most requested fields (biomarker_name, biomarker_unit, biomarker_value, disease_response_os, ecog_performance_status, tumor measurements) are not applicable and were correctly marked as not_reported.

The schema appears designed for clinical oncology or biomarker studies, but this paper is a metagenomic assembly and microbial diversity characterization study. Only feces_phenotype_value and host_species contain relevant data.

The feces_phenotype_value field was populated with microbiome prevalence and abundance data, which is the closest relevant information to fecal phenotype in this paper, but this paper does not report traditional phenotypic measurements.
